items.title: Beating the frontier on NetHack
items.summary: games, testing
items.content:
November 13, 2026 | Paul Ryan , Member of Technical Staff | Mikail Khan , Research intern | Will Wilson , Co-founder and CEO

That’s not quite true for computer game history (though NetHack was very early and very influential ), but it’s true for the history of Antithesis. The company started when I got lunch with Dave and said: “let’s make the FDB simulator but for everything ” and he was like: “no, let’s make a fuzzer so smart it can beat NetHack,” and then we gradually realized that we were actually talking about the same thing.

In the years that followed, NetHack continued to inspire and challenge us. The first Antithesis VCS repo (long since deleted) was called “fuzzhack” because it was a fuzzer for NetHack. Before we built our deterministic hypervisor , we tried Hermit-style deterministic Linux userland because it’s the bare minimum you need to beat NetHack. NetHack inspired our thinking about the importance of strategy , about the importance of code coverage and also about its inadequacy, and about why you need intrinsic curiosity rewards to have any hope of applying AI to this problem. NetHack inspired many of our early experiments in visualization. Wanting to interactively explore NetHack performance and coverage maps is why we wrote the first version of the reactive notebook that now powers our UI. Processing reams of NetHack data that wouldn’t fit in memory was why we decided to put a GCP subscription on my credit card so we could crunch the data in BigQuery, which later led us to invent skip trees , and finally Pangolin .

All of this is because it was a worthy adversary – perhaps even what my colleague David MacIver likes to call a “dragon problem.” NetHack is famously difficult for human beings because it combines permadeath, extreme information scarcity (reading the source code of the game to figure out how to beat it is practically a rite of passage for aficionados), and a brutal intolerance for error. But it’s also very difficult for autonomous systems like fuzzers and AI agents due to its sprawling state space and to the need for long-horizon planning to make any real progress. People have written bots that have successfully beaten the game, but despite Meta’s investment in the NetHack Learning Environment , AI agents have struggled with it. The wins that both the hardcoded bots and the AIs (most recently GPT-6 Astra) have eked out have been skin-of-their-teeth affairs involving lucky seeds and “beginner-friendly” roles. Nobody has produced a system that can reliably and quickly beat the game over and over again as any character build.

“Beginner-friendly” by NetHack standards, at least.

Antithesis can now find a path to victory within 5 wall-clock minutes on nearly 80% of NetHack seeds. Moreover, the median time to victory within the seeds that finish is under 2 minutes. To explain how we did this, we need to let you in on a secret: Antithesis is not just a system for unopinionated state space exploration, it is also something akin to a probabilistic programming language, a new computing paradigm for partially describing tests or other tasks and letting search and optimization fill in the rest. When you put this tool in the hands of capable AI agents, they can do things like beat NetHack in 30 seconds. But first… back to our story.

The game is considered one of the hardest games in the world, with winning episodes lasting hundreds of thousands of steps, and a permadeath setting that starts agents at the beginning in a whole new world if they die in the dungeon. – Insights from the NeurIPS 2021 NetHack Challenge , Hambro et al.

The overall goal of NetHack is straightforward to state, if not to achieve. You begin on the top floor of a dungeon; your objective, the Amulet of Yendor, is at the bottom, in Moloch’s Sanctum. items.title: Your Cryptography Conspiracy Theory Is Wrong - Dhole Moments
items.content:
This conversation plays out hundreds of times a day, but (thankfully) only a handful of those involve me:

Cryptography nerd: “Oh, you probably want to use [sensible recommendation].”

Person: “Ah, well, can I really trust that? The NSA probably backdoored it 30 years ago. Dual_EC, amirite?!”

Koblitz and Menezes, unheard: “ You fucking wot m8? “

Conspiracy theories about the NSA and/or NIST are a dime a dozen these days. And, ever since the Snowden disclosures in 2013, I am politically primed to directionally agree with distrusting the US government wholesale.

But most of the technical arguments baked into folks’ conspiracy theories make no goddamn sense .

This distrust is not exclusive to only the US government.

The goal of this blog post is not to convince you that you should trust any government; just that they are not magical or omniscient.

To that end, I’m going to explore some of the history of NSA, NIST, and cryptography standardization. Then, to explore some of the conspiracy theories that were being floated about such activity, and what we’ve learned in the years since (especially in the past month). Finally, I’m going to examine some of the current conspiracy theories floating around message boards and social media today, and explain why they’re almost certainly wrong.

Buckle up, this is going to be a tedious one.

If you find yourself asking a question like this, the correct answer is simply, “You shouldn’t.”

After all, I have never held (let alone even applied for) a security clearance, and have no access to any non-public information. I’m also not a current or former government employee, and have no aspirations to ever become one. I have access to all the same facts anyone else does.

In balance, I have no horse in the race of who trusts whom. I’m just tired of hearing the same poorly reasoned arguments all the damn time, and would like to stop having to repeat myself when I encounter one.

The sources for this, by the way, are the declassified United States Senate Select Committee on Intelligence and United States Cryptologic History .

The Data Encryption Standard (DES) was published in the Federal Register in 1975 and then standardized in 1977.

We consider it weak these days, but DES was a real game-changer for its time: It offered a standard block cipher to use for sensitive (but not classified) commercial applications. Prior to DES, the history of cryptography was largely about military uses (except a few quirky mathematicians here and there), going back before Caesar’s cipher .

From declassified documents, we now know the full story, but from the time that DES was first standardized, up until recent years, there have been a concerns about NSA’s involvement .

We sent the S-boxes off to Washington. They came back and were all different.

Alan Konheim, quoted in Applied Cryptography , p. 280

To say that academics did not trust DES would be putting it mildly: Martin Hellman (who, with Whitfield Diffie and Ralph Merkle, invented public-key cryptography) sent a letter in 1975 to the National Bureau of Standards that stated:

Whit Diffie and I have become concerned that the proposed data encryption standard, while probably secure against commercial assault, may be extremely vulnerable to attack by an intelligence organization.

Martin Hellman, re-published in this paper in 1990.

At the heart of the concern about DES was something called an S-box, which simply maps an input to an output, but whose purpose is to provide a non-linear transformation to obscure the relationship between the ciphertext and the key.

The S-box used by DES was chosen by NSA. This led a lot of people to suspect there was a backdoor in the selection of the S-boxes for DES. It turned out to be the opposite, of course : The NSA had discovered differential cryptanalysis in secret, and had selected S-boxes that were resistant to this technique, but did not want to reveal it publicly (lest they lose their advantage over rival…

items.title: systemd Gets Built-In System Reporting With systemd-report
items.content:
systemd is getting a new reporting subsystem designed to collect both static system information and dynamic runtime metrics in one place.

Called systemd-report , the new tool gathers data from multiple metric provider services via a generic Varlink interface and combines it into a single timestamped JSON report. The work targets system and fleet management, where administrators need a consistent view of many machines.

The collected information is split into two groups. The first covers relatively static system “facts,” such as CPU architecture, hostname, kernel version, OS identification, installed RAM, CPU count, virtualization technology, TPM information, and other hardware or platform details.

The second covers changing runtime metrics like CPU and memory use, load averages, disk I/O, swap usage, system pressure, cgroup statistics, network interface states, systemd unit states, restart counters, queued jobs, and high-priority journal messages.

According to Lennart Poettering, the underlying metrics service was initially contributed by Meta with a focus on dynamic runtime information. The same interface was later extended to handle more static system facts as well, something Amutable is using for areas such as operating system deployment management.

Once gathered, systemd-report compiles all of this information into a consistent snapshot representing the state of the machine at a particular point in time.

The subsystem is designed for remote fleet management. Reports can be uploaded directly to an HTTPS server using PUT requests, letting organizations send system information to a central control plane. The setup includes periodic uploads via a systemd timer and reports triggered by events like system boot, reboot, or shutdown.

For security, reports can be cryptographically signed before being sent, and systemd currently provides three signing methods.

The simplest uses a software-generated asymmetric key stored locally. Systems with TPM hardware can produce a TPM quote covering platform measurements and the report data. A third option supports confidential-computing environments by generating a CPU TSM quote that ties the report to measurements of the secure virtual machine.

This makes systemd-report different from traditional monitoring tools like Prometheus and its node_exporter . While both expose similar information, systemd obtains data directly from lower-level OS components instead of relying on a separate scraping model.

More importantly, systemd-report focuses on complete, signed, timestamped snapshots rather than independent streams of metrics. Poettering notes that the two approaches are not mutually exclusive, and the new infrastructure could eventually provide the basis for integration between them.

The architecture is also intentionally extensible. Third-party projects can provide additional metrics or signing mechanisms simply by exposing the appropriate Varlink socket. These providers can be written in any programming language and only need to implement a small interface.

In other words, systemd-report is not just another command for displaying system information. It is shaping up as a broader reporting framework built directly into systemd, combining system facts, runtime metrics, secure signing, and remote reporting in a format suitable for managing everything from individual Linux machines to large server fleets.

For additional details, see Poettering’s announcement .

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.title: ML Modules for Mere Mortals
items.summary: ml, plt
items.content:
I think everyone can agree code needs to be modular.

Modularity lets us reason locally about our code no matter how big it grows.

However, no one seems to agree on how code should be modular.

There are a bunch of different approaches and each new language seems to bring their own spin on it.

Today we’re going to talk about a pretty old spin: ML Modules.

ML here stands for Meta Language, as seen in SML and OCaml (and not machine learning).

Despite SML first appearing in 1983, ML Modules have not caught on.

OCaml is the sole production language you’ll find with an ML module system, and at the height of its popularity it’s niche.

This is a shame because ML modules have a lot to offer.

We’re going to talk about what ML modules are and then touch a little on why ML modules are.

Who better after all to explain modules, than the guy who doesn’t know what’s in a module

Modules exist to make our code modular, duh, but what does that mean in practice?

I think most programmers have some intuitive sense of modularity:

Most languages have a way to do this, and if they don’t, one gets created for them (looking at you JavaScript).

ML modules achieves this with, you guessed it, the Module.

ML modules, however, are a little different from the modules we know and love.

To explain their differences, we’ll lean on a made-up Rust-inspired syntax.

It will start off looking a little weird and gradually, as we introduce concepts, end up looking really weird (but hopefully more familiar than SML syntax).

We’ll start by defining a module with just functions:

AModule bundles together related arithmetic functions as one thing we can reason about.

Each function can see every other function in the module.

This is useful, but any language with namespaces offers this.

A little more unique is that ML modules will let us put not only function definitions in modules, but also type definitions:

Here we have a Set module with a Set type, which is a sorted Vec<i32> .

Our module’s functions can refer to the type definitions much the same way they can refer to their module’s function definitions.

Okay but that’s not that crazy, still well within the realm of Rust modules.

Not only can modules contain type definitions.

A module type is called a signature (so we don’t get it confused with “normal” types).

A module signature declares every definition of a module alongside its type.

This might look similar to the way we define a trait in Rust.

That’s because much like traits act as interfaces in Rust, signatures act as interfaces in ML Modules.

Modules having signatures is the single most important thing to understand about ML Modules.

All the complexity and expressiveness of modules results from them having signatures and the wonderful wacky things that enables.

Signatures resemble the way a C/C++ implementation file conforms to its header.

Modules, unlike .cc files, aren’t in a 1:1 relationship with signatures.

Our Set module can conform to any signature that it matches.

A module matches a signature when it defines every declaration in the signature and they agree on type.

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

items.title: Commerce Dept to block Chinese companies from renting advanced chips in overseas data centers
items.content:
Jensen Huang scandal trail leads to Alibaba, the king of free Chinese AI: Chart of the Day

Fri, November 13, 2026 at 8:00 p.m. GMT+9 3 min read

The cheapest way for an American company to run AI is a free model made in China. The scandal that just cost Nvidia its CEO could shut off the chips those models depend on.

Companies are making the switch fast. Duolingo ( DUOL ) co-founder and CEO Luis von Ahn said at Yahoo Finance Invest on Thursday that each AI practice call in his app used to cost about 30 cents. Now it's "less than a cent," he said, "by moving most of this to open weight models ," the kind of AI anyone can download and run for free. Decagon co-founder and CEO Jesse Zhang said new customers at his AI startup run "almost entirely" on them.

The most downloaded of those free models come from China, and the biggest maker by far is Alibaba ( BABA ).

Economist Nouriel Roubini says China's edge rests on two shortcuts that are closing fast. Chinese open models are about 95% as good as American ones, the NYU Stern professor emeritus said at Invest, because "we allowed distillation — that's over — and we allowed them through Singapore to get all these advanced chips." Distillation is when one AI model learns by copying a stronger model's answers.

Alibaba stock fell 7% Thursday to its lowest close since January 2025 as reports circulated that Washington is moving to shut down that Singapore route. The company reports earnings Nov. 19.

NYSE - Nasdaq Real Time Price • USD (BABA)

Alibaba's free AI models, called Qwen, get about half of the downloads that can be traced to a maker on Hugging Face , the biggest online library of AI models, by Yahoo Finance calculations. That's more than twice as many as Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ), OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ), Meta ( META ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), and Nvidia ( NVDA ) combined.

Hugging Face, Yahoo Finance "Right now there is massive usage of ... a Chinese family called Qwen, which is the most used one," Hugging Face co-founder Thomas Wolf said on Deirdre Bosa Live this week.

Meta used to own this race. Its Llama 4 and Alibaba's Qwen3 came out the same month in 2025. Developers have since downloaded Qwen3 more than 20 times as often on Ollama, a popular app for running AI on your own computer.

Ollama, Yahoo Finance How the Nvidia scandal reaches Alibaba

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after admitting to an affair with a woman US intelligence officials believe passed information to Beijing, according to reports . She has been identified as Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore company that rents out computing power built on Nvidia chips.

Alibaba was Megaspeed's founding customer and is still its biggest, the Financial Times reported . The US investigation targets Megaspeed, not Alibaba, and Megaspeed denies diverting chips.

Financial Times, The Information, Culper Research, Yahoo Finance China can't legally buy Nvidia's most advanced chips, so renting them abroad has been the workaround. Now the Commerce Department is finalizing a rule that would bar Chinese AI companies from using advanced chips in data centers outside China, including in Singapore and Malaysia, The Information reported .

The scandal also cost America's open-source AI its loudest booster. "Jensen was a great champion for open weight," Zhang said, adding that "there's still a gap between the open-source frontier in the US and in China." And China hawks in Washington now have an opening to press their case.

Roubini thinks Washington's crackdown will flip that gap. Without copying American models and without the Singapore chips, he said, China's AI makers are "going to lag behind us."

Internal AI tools helped analyze interview transcripts, research, and draft this post. Humans reviewed, edited, and fact-checked this post before publication.

Jared Blikre is the global markets and data editor for Yahoo Finance. Follow him on X at @SPYJared or email him at jaredblikre@yahooinc.com.

items.title: Three new Ophiostoma fungi from South Korean oak trees
items.content:
Three New Ophiostoma Fungal Species Discovered on South Korean Oak Trees

A targeted mycological field survey conducted within native oak stands in Sancheong, Republic of Korea, has uncovered three previously undescribed species of wood-inhabiting fungi belonging to the genus Ophiostoma. The newly documented fungal lineages, formally designated as Ophiostoma querceti, Ophiostoma guttiferum, and Ophiostoma subcorticale, were repeatedly recovered from fresh natural wounds on three indigenous oak species: Quercus mongolica, Quercus variabilis, and Quercus acutissima. By integrating multi-gene phylogenetic reconstructions with rigorous micromorphological and physiological examinations, a research team led by H.G. Woo, D.Hyeon Lee, and S.E. Cho confirmed that these isolates form a well-supported, distinct evolutionary lineage residing directly within the Ophiostoma ulmi species complex.

The genus Ophiostoma, classified within the order Ophiostomatales of the Ascomycota, comprises an ecologically diverse assemblage of wood-inhabiting fungi frequently associated with commercial sapstain or blue stain in processed timber. Historically, species in this genus, together with Ceratocystis species, have been grouped as ophiostomatoid fungi due to convergent adaptations for insect-mediated dispersal, characterized by dark, globose fruiting bodies bearing prolonged necks topped with sticky spore masses. Modern phylogenetic analyses have firmly separated Ophiostoma from Ceratocystis into distinct ascomycetous orders, yet both groups remain deeply tied to forest ecosystems through interactions with wood-infesting arthropods. In particular, phloem-feeding bark beetles belonging to the subfamily Scolytinae, including species of Scolytus, serve as primary dispersal vectors by carrying sticky conidia and ascospores directly between tree stems. The vulnerability of domestic tree populations was recently underscored when Ophiostoma novo-ulmi was formally identified in South Korea in 2022, causing escalating mortality across regional elm populations and triggering nationwide initiatives to survey potential arboreal pathogens.

Field sampling took place from April to November 2025 across a natural oak forest located in Danseong-myeon, Sancheong-gun, situated at geographical coordinates 35°16’26.80″N, 127°51’33.421″E. The investigating team inspected fresh stem wounds, specifically targeting injuries less than one month old, on mature specimens of Quercus mongolica, Quercus variabilis, and Quercus acutissima using a 10× hand lens to detect characteristic reproductive structures. Subcortical wood and bark tissues bearing visible fungal growth were transported in labeled paper bags to the laboratory, where single-spore isolations were performed from germinating conidia or ascospores to establish axenic cultures. Representative living isolates were accessioned into the Culture Collection of Chungnam National University under codes CDH138, CDH139, and CDH242, along with their respective authentic cultures. Holotype specimens were formally deposited in the herbarium collection of the Korea National Arboretum in Pocheon, while permanent ex-holotype cultures were preserved in the Korean Agricultural Culture Collection of the National Academy of Agricultural Science in Wanju under accession numbers KACC 411103, KACC 411104, and KACC 411342.

To rigorously verify the taxonomic identities of the recovered isolates, genomic DNA was extracted from mycelia harvested from two-week-old axenic cultures using a commercial purification kit. Molecular delimitation relied on the polymerase chain reaction amplification and bidirectional Sanger sequencing of four diagnostic nuclear loci: the internal transcribed spacer ribosomal RNA region using primers ITS1F and ITS4, the beta-tubulin gene using primers T10 and Bt2b, partial translation elongation factor 1-alpha sequences using EF1F and EF2R, and the second largest subunit of RNA polymerase II using primers RPB2-5f2 and…

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Big tech is here to let us down
items.content:
When I woke up this morning I thought about writing about the ongoing drama surrounding Nvidia and its morally and ethically corrupt leader. But, then I quickly saw the news about Microsoft Outlook going down, and with it Teams and Copilot.

I soon saw many employees celebrating what effectively became a "snow day for adults" as they literally couldn't do their jobs. Then I started seeing various businesses, ranging from small to medium, saying that their normal support services are unsurprisingly not working and instead to contact them via social media. Except, it's not just businesses that are impacted by Microsoft's incompetence. Even if this is some legitimate accident (and not a more likely instance of someone vibecoding their way via Copilot), when a company like Microsoft fires tens of thousands of employees, including many engineers, then these problems are not only more likely, but also more difficult to quickly fix. The fact that this has actually been an issue across two separate days is pathetic for a company like Microsoft.

As beyond businesses impacted, all sorts of other entities have been impacted. Various forms of educational institutions from schools to universities as well as the courts! I wouldn't be surprised if healthcare has been impacted as well.

Now, are Microsoft going to offer any compensation for either lost business or additional accrued costs? I highly doubt it, even though it is literally their fault and they do still have the cash reserves, despite increasingly wasting it on loss-making AI adventures.

This is a reminder of how indebted the Global North has become to Microsoft and its enshittified services. If most (but thankfully not all) businesses and institutions are deep into Microsoft systems, then when Microsoft inevitably messes up again, large swathes of organisations will not be able to function properly. Yes, it might be good for the individual worker in a generic office role, but for keyworker type organisations this can have really damaging implications. Many European state institutions have already started the move away from Microsoft to open source alternatives. Largely to not be at the mercy of an inconsistent United States of America, but also for times like this. As when Microsoft services go down, you cannot fix it! You have to wait for Microsoft to find a competent employee who wasn't let go to try and fix what was broken by some inept leftover who was deluded enough to think that Copilot can do everything.

I still want to talk about the issues of the impact of other US company Nvidia and the implications it has around the world. But that can wait for another day. Plus, who knows if another affairs comes out (we're currently at three).

items.title: Someone's impersonating this blog
items.summary: security
items.content:
I was googling the name of my website, as one does occasionally, and was surprised to see a link to one of my blog posts on mataroa.site . At first I figured it was just an alternate domain name for mataroa.blog , but no, when you type mataroa.site into your browser, it shows you my blog . It's the only thing that's hosted there.

My next thought was that someone bought me a URL, but that can't be the case either: using a custom domain on mataroa requires a premium account, which I don't have. For anything but a plain redirect, I would have needed to set up the A record my end.

I then realized that the version of my blog on that site doesn't have the latest post . The most recent update on the homepage is my Aug 21 entry . When you scroll down and start clicking some of the older links, you get 404 pages. You also get a 404 if you try to post a comment, load the RSS feed or view standalone pages like the AI statement .

Someone scraped my blog and created a website to impersonate me. They're also impersonating mataroa , since using the name implies some sort of official connection.

They're re-hosting the stolen images on their own server, and they all have a watermark. Bizarrely, the watermark is mattbee.mataroa.blog , my real URL. I assume this is to somehow make it seem legitimate, like it's an officially-sanctioned mirror, but I don't know who they think is going to care. It's not like they're stealing from a site with name recognition.

When you view the source of a blog post, it's identical to the rendered HTML except that there are two Cloudflare scripts at the bottom, one to obfuscate the mailto: link in the footer (which doesn't work 1 ) and one for analytics.

When you view the source of the index, there's a hidden link at the bottom to a Chinese github.io page for a website cloning tool.

I have no idea why I was targeted for impersonation. It should be obvious this isn't a high-value website. 2 It's a personal blog where I write what's relevant to me, and that rarely overlaps with anything other people care about. If the subject matter didn't tip them off, it should be clear from the 0 comments on most posts that this is not an enterprise ripe for monetization.

If they just wanted a fake blog to scam adsense, surely a large language model would happily spew out more SEO-friendly slop than anything I have to offer. If their goal was to leech off the popularity of mataroa, why not impersonate one of the blogs with multiple front-page appearances on the orange website? Surely they have more SEO juice than me. Nothing about this makes any sense.

Anyway, the URL is registered with Namecheap, so I sent them an abuse report . I have no idea if they'll act on it. They don't seem to have a good track record of giving a shit unless the content is actually hosted with them.

It's hosted with Cloudflare, and the abuse reporting form they insist you use straight-up doesn't work . Click "Submit an abuse report" and it'll take you to a completely blank page. Very encouraging.

I'd have to dox myself to do a DMCA takedown, and I don't have the legal resources to do anything when it gets ignored. So if neither evil corporation cares to do anything, I guess I can just get fucked. I figure the best thing I can do to protect myself is document everything here. If you see a link to mataroa.site , it's not affiliated with me or mataroa. It seems like it isn't set up to scam people or distribute malware at the moment, but it probably will in the future. Be careful.

The index page also has a meta tag with a verification code for mitgo.com , a fake-looking website with some word salad identifying it as some kind of ad/SEO scamming platform or service. Will try to investigate this further.

It does, I had just forgotten to enable javascript.  ↩

items.title: Instagram Meta AI Vulnerability: How Hackers Bypassed 2FA with Prompt Injection
items.content:
Update 5: Instagram is now leaking recovery email and phone numbers linked to an account.

Seems like every day a new security issue crops up at Instagram.

Instagram Exposing Linked Email and Phone Number

Update 4: A new report suggests that Instagram accounts may be vulnerable to coordinated mass-report abuse. According to the claim, when a newly created account is routed through a Los Angeles-based VPN and then submits a specific mix of reports in scam and fraud category, the targeted account can allegedly be banned without any human review.

Instagram Account Banning by AI by Reporting Scam and Fraud (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 3: Meta’s apparent fix for the AI bot vulnerability is difficult to take seriously. Instead of fully disabling the risky functionality, they reportedly removed it from the visible interface while leaving the underlying API endpoint accessible. Hiding the button may stop regular users from seeing the feature, but it does nothing if attackers can still reach the same workflow directly through the API.

items.content:
New York City Council Approves Landmark Legislation Banning Surveillance Pricing

Speaker Julie Menin’s legislation will prevent companies from using personal data to offer different prices to different New Yorkers

Council also passes legislative package in honor of Veterans Day, including property tax exemption for seriously disabled veterans

NEW YORK – Today, the New York City Council approved major legislation that will ban surveillance pricing in the five boroughs. The bill, sponsored by Speaker Julie Menin, will prevent companies from using New Yorkers’ personal data and algorithms to sell goods and services at different prices to different consumers, and is among the strongest surveillance pricing bans in the country.

In honor of Veterans Day, the Council also approved a package of bills aimed at improving life for New York City veterans. The package includes two bills that will improve housing access and affordability for veterans: one granting a full property tax exemption for the primary residence of permanently and totally disabled veterans, and the other requiring the Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) to conduct an annual report on veteran occupancy in city-run Mitchell-Lama housing. A third bill in the package would establish a permanent LGBTQ+ liaison within the Department of Veterans’ Services (DVS).

Watch Speaker Menin’s pre-Stated press conference here and the Council’s Stated Meeting here . Photos will be available here .

Banning Surveillance Pricing in New York City

Introduction 891-A, sponsored by Speaker Julie Menin, would prohibit any entity or service provider from engaging in surveillance pricing, defined as pricing set completely or in part by algorithm that uses personal data to offer different prices to different customers for the same goods or services.

“The City Council is putting consumers first by ending the deceptive and insidious practice of surveillance pricing,” said Speaker Julie Menin. “When corporations use algorithms and personal data to charge different people different prices for the same products, it’s unethical and worsens our affordability crisis. We take consumer protection extremely seriously, and we will continue fighting to lower prices and stop predatory corporate tactics.”

Surveillance pricing is invisible to consumers, making it difficult to identify, but reports suggest the practice is occurring in a variety of industries. One investigation found that a major grocery delivery platform was engaging in algorithmic pricing experiments that resulted in individualized price differences as high as 23 percent. Another investigation found that the price of a television at one retailer increased from $499.99 to $599.99 when the consumer pulled into the store’s parking lot. A behavioral economist who worked for a major ride-share company revealed that the application increases prices when a consumer’s phone battery is low because they might not otherwise be able to get home if they do not accept the high offer. The Council aims to end these predatory practices and protect New York consumers with this landmark ban.

items.title: No AI Slop: A Manifesto
items.content:
Written by the speakers and attendees of AIE Code Summit 2026

In 2001, 17 software engineers and leaders got together at a ski lodge in Snowbird, Utah to understand the biggest challenge of their time: heavyweight, documentation-driven software development processes.

Out of this we got the Agile Manifesto , four values and twelve principles that changed how most of the industry builds software.

Today we convene to build our own manifesto - the No AI Slop manifesto.

AI increasingly helps us write our code, docs, plans, and messages. We've all been on the receiving end of slop, and most of us have sent some too. Through this work, we have come to value:

Our own thinking over a model's first draft

Improving the system over patching the output

The world moves especially fast these days, but the goal of these resolutions is to embrace our important human role in harnessing AI safely, responsibly, in a way that creates value for everyone, and that will be relevant for years to come.

AI is the most useful tool most of us have ever worked with, but a swarm of agents can produce more work in a single day than a person can review in our lifetime.

Slop is when we put less effort into producing something than we ask the consumer to spend understanding it.

Using AI doesn't necessarily make something slop. Slop happens when we pass AI output along without taking responsibility for the quality or the reader's experience.

AI cannot replace human judgement, it can only amplify our judgement (or lack thereof).

Slop is asymmetric. The cost of producing a thousand-line PR or a ten-page doc is approaching zero, while the cost of reviewing it remains constant.

In code, even before AI, slop proliferates when we repeatedly work around problems instead of solving them correctly. It comes from tools that lean HEAVILY toward adding rather than subtracting.

A lot of slop comes from pressure. Companies are pushing their people to redefine what is humanly possible.

Slop compounds. The more slop sits in our knowledge base, in chat, in code, the more of it the next agent reads and copies.

The more slop flying around a team, the more we lose the will to fight it. Communication and quality get worse over time, not better.

Human time and attention is incredibly valuable, so we optimize for using it wisely.

We fight slop because AI should make our work better, not just easier.

We optimize systems, tools, and products for efficient elicitation of human intent and for efficient human understanding.

We do our own thinking when working with a model. We explore resources, code, and prior art to truly understand the problem before the work starts.

We own the intent, taste, and consequences of what we ship, however much AI helps us make it.

When an agent wrote something we're sending, we make that clear, and we check the parts that matter before it goes out.

When someone sends us slop, we tell them, kindly, and ask them to review it first. Most of us have needed that same note at some point.

There will always be alpha in reviewing something . As models improve, we may stop reading most of the code. We may still review a plan, design, or result, because if we don't, we just get the same output as everyone else.

Agent reviews, linters, and verifiers are useful but not sufficent. For now, we still review at least some subset of the outputs. What subset depends on the stakes.

What shipped, who's using it, and how it's helping them matters FAR MORE than lines of code, prs merged, tokens spent, or the number of agents running in parallel.

Unreviewed output isn't always necessarily bad. One-shot prompts and vibe coding are high leverage tools. "Slop" is bad when it undermines our outcome -- a useful product, a maintainable system, or saving ourselves and our teammates time and energy.

When a mistake shows up twice, we scale ourselves and our team by improving the system and its guardrails. Anything a linter, type checker, or automated check can…

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

BitLocker는 Microsoft가 제공하는 전체 볼륨 암호화 기술로, 신뢰할 수 있는 플랫폼 모듈(TPM)에 저장된 복호화 키 없이는 디스크 접근이 불가능하도록 설계되었다. 많은 조직과 정부 계약업체에서 필수 보호 기술로 사용 중이다. YellowKey 익스플로잇의 핵심은 커스텀으로 만들어진 FsTx 폴더 사용으로, fstx.dll과 관련된 디렉터리는 Microsoft의 transactional NTFS 기술을 활용한다.

items.title: CBC tested 6 popular apps to see what data they collect and share.
items.content:
Whether you are buying a coffee, groceries, checking the weather or unwinding with an online video, there’s a free mobile app for just about everything.

But a Marketplace investigation shows the cost of this convenience is your privacy – and the data you’re sharing goes far beyond what you might realize.

Marketplace tested six of the most popular Android and iOS apps in Canada — Tim Hortons, PC Optimum, the Weather Network, Facebook, Amazon and YouTube — to find out what data they collect and where it goes.

To do so, Joel Reardon, an associate professor in the department of computer science, and his team at the University of Calgary scanned the network traffic of the apps on an Android device. Privo, an organization that evaluates apps to ensure they comply with U.S. child privacy laws, also did a scan of the apps on iOS, Apple’s operating system.

While doing scans to see the network traffic of mobile apps on Android, some apps appeared to be sending information to outside companies around the world. The network scan above shows the activity from all the apps on someone’s phone, not necessarily the apps Marketplace tested. (CBC)

In their user policies, the apps we tested explicitly disclose that they collect or share certain data and that when you use the app, you accept their terms.

But Reardon and Celeste Rollason, an independent analyst who used to work with Privo, are concerned some apps collect more than they need and are sharing what they learn with others around the world.

That data ranges from your name and email address to your exact whereabouts.

“To me, this is not the internet we wanted. This is not the internet we deserve. It's turned into a monstrous data collection surveillance system,” Reardon said.

Here’s what we learned about each app we tested, and what you can do to protect your data.

The scan showed that the Tim Hortons app appeared to be sending data to third-party companies as soon as you launch it.

Reardon said one overseas third-party company built into the app appeared to be receiving enough information to create the equivalent of a digital fingerprint for each device, so it can be identified in the future.

Rollason said the third party brands itself as a fraud protection service. She noted the amount of data collected “seems quite excessive” to validate the purchase of a cup of coffee.

Marketplace isn’t identifying any of the third-party companies or their locations because accountability rests with the app developer.

In a statement, Tim Hortons’ director of communications Michael Oliveira said this third party only collects this information for “fraud prevention, account protection, and payment abuse prevention, not for marketing or advertising … or to work around guests’ choices regarding those activities.”

Oliveira said the information collected can help detect if a never-before-seen device is being used on a customer’s account or if a “threat actor” is pretending to be a customer.

He also said the third party is not allowed to sell the data and that Tim Hortons does not sell users’ personal information to third-party companies or data brokers.

The test showed the PC Optimum app appeared to be sending 10 outside companies information about which products users are searching for — even if the product was sensitive like a search for prenatal vitamins.

One third-party company appeared to be receiving a user’s latitude and longitude and an identifier unique to the device.

items.title: How Cloudflare uses QuePaxa—a leaderless, fault-detection-free consensus algorithm—for its global control plane
items.content:
Cloudflare recently announced Meerkat , an experimental distributed consensus service designed to manage our internal global control plane. It is powered by a new consensus algorithm published by researchers Tennage & Băsescu et al. called QuePaxa (2023).

QuePaxa is an unusual choice; most consensus systems use well-established consensus algorithms like Raft, (Multi-)Paxos or Viewstamped Replication. These algorithms are well understood, have mature implementations, and usually work well.

Unfortunately, common consensus algorithms often suffer in wide-area networks with volatile network connectivity and latency, i.e., networks like the Internet, which is where Meerkat runs. These algorithms rely on a single leader process being available and having predictable latency. If the leader goes down, experiences higher latency than usual, or is disconnected, the entire consensus system slows down or becomes unavailable until the leader is replaced. This is unacceptable for Meerkat.

Meerkat’s global deployment environment led us to a newer consensus algorithm, QuePaxa, which promises better stability despite volatility, in large part by not relying on a leader to make progress. In this post we’ll explain why we chose QuePaxa and how the QuePaxa algorithm works.

Meerkat is a distributed system in which replicas agree upon an ordered log of events, where each event is decided by a consensus algorithm.

Consensus algorithms allow a group of machines to agree on a single shared truth, even if some of those machines crash or disconnect. Consensus algorithms provide an important guarantee: machines never decide conflicting values. This ensures Meerkat replicas’ logs never diverge.

Meerkat uses its consensus-powered log to expose applications   like a key-value store, where each entry in the log is a get  or a put . Because the consensus algorithm guarantees replicas’ logs never diverge, they all construct the same key-value (KV) state. Comparable consensus-powered systems include Consul, etcd, and Apache ZooKeeper.

Unlike similar systems, however, Meerkat was designed for global scale . A Meerkat cluster may be distributed across continents and connected by links that often exhibit high and variable latency. This is an unusual setup for consensus systems, which are usually deployed in smaller, more local networks, and have strict latency requirements .

The challenges of consensus at a global scale

While all consensus algorithms ensure that replicas agree on the same value, many of them become disproportionately unavailable or slow when network conditions degrade (but machines do not crash). We have seen this happen firsthand: in 2020, the partial failure  of a core Cloudflare network switch caused a consensus-powered system to degrade and the dashboard to operate 80x slower than usual, for six hours. Critically, the system lost no data. But it became unavailable for writes until the issue was resolved, which is unacceptable.

Ideally, a consensus algorithm should be able to make progress despite latency spikes and broken connections, not just replica failures. This is particularly a problem at global scale, where faults are more likely to originate in the network, and not our own servers.

Let’s examine two common traits of consensus algorithms that can lead to degradation under hostile network conditions: destructive interference and fault detection. Later, we’ll see how QuePaxa sidesteps both of these issues.

Consider Paxos, the veritable grandfather of most consensus algorithms. A lot of consensus algorithms inherit the structure of Paxos – both the good and the not-so-good  bits.

Leaving an egregious amount   of detail out, here’s how Paxos works. There are two kinds of processes: proposers and acceptors. 온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-128132 📢 Source: GitHub_M 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False AIOHTTP is an asynchronous HTTP client/server framework for asyncio and Python. Prior to 3.14.4, the WebSocket reader continues parsing frames already received after the receive queue pauses the transport, and empty messages are not counted toward the queue size. With permessage-deflate, one read of compressed frames can add many megabytes of decompressed messages to the receive queue. A remote peer can send many small or compressed messages faster than the application consumes them and cause excessive memory use in a server or client. This issue is fixed in version 3.14.4. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-13T20:42:17.871Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-128132
